name: Maximum-Generated Classes Are Closed Under Nonempty One-Coordinate Fiber Products
statement: If two maximum-generated classes have exactly one shared coordinate and otherwise disjoint coordinate sets, then every nonempty coordinate fiber product is maximum-generated.
proof: Prepare independent maximum parents so their marked reductions, one-height layers, and outside words occupy prescribed consecutive maximum-sequence levels. On the product of their private extensions, add the shared coordinate and one control coordinate. Explicit four-, three-, one-, and zero-point control fibers depend on the two entry levels and required heights. Vandermonde and Pascal identities give the Sauer cardinality at the sum rank, and missing traces rule out every support one larger. Fixing the two original marks and the new control recovers the fiber product.
